in_hebrew.name: שולםזנה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew words 'shulam' (peace, completeness) and 'zana' (adorned, ornament). The name means 'grace, beauty, adorned.' Suzzana is a variant of Susanna, and is mentioned in the apocryphal Book of Daniel.

in_greek.name: Σουσαννή
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'sousa' (help) and 'ané' (grace). The name means 'grace, help.' Susanna is a character in Greek literature and also appears in the apocryphal Book of Daniel.

in_latin.name: Susanna
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'sus' (grace) and 'anna' (lily). The name means 'grace, lily.' Susanna is a character in Latin literature and also appears in the apocryphal Book of Daniel.

biblical_reference.note: In the apocryphal Book of Daniel, Susanna (or Suzzana) is a beautiful and virtuous wife of Joakim, who is falsely accused of adultery by two elders. Daniel intervenes and saves Susanna from their false accusations, revealing the true motives of the elders.
